5.0.0.en: The Apostle directs his recommendations to the shepherds, who are the bishops and priests, whom he gathers in the word "elders," which in Greek is "presbyteros," meaning bishops or priests, as it occurs in Greek in (Acts 20:17, 28). He speaks with humility and says "their fellow elder" and not their superior, to show his sympathy with them, for he suffers the sufferings of persecution as they do and awaits the glories of heaven with them. He is an eyewitness of the sufferings of Christ, His crucifixion and His resurrection, which he preaches.

5.1.0.en: Overseers: that is, supervisors, and he means the bishops, because the word bishop means overseer.

5.1.1.en: The Apostle Peter summarizes his recommendations as follows:

5.1.2.en: 1- Shepherding the children of God: he directs their attention to the fact that their people are God's flock and they are stewards over it, so that they may be faithful before Him in their shepherding of His people.

5.1.3.en: 2- Willingly: he asks them for vigilance, oversight and care for the people, not as a heavy duty to which they are compelled, but they strive with love, by their own choice, to care for every individual.

5.1.4.en: 3- Free service: they should have no material greed behind the service, but with love and zeal they serve for the sake of God.

5.2.0.en: 4- Not lording it over: they do not exploit their position as shepherds to domineer over the money of the Church and use it according to their own wishes, but with wisdom they listen to the opinions of those who help them and fulfill the wishes of their people.

5.2.1.en: 5- Being an example: in all their words and actions, so that the servants and the people may follow their example.

5.3.0.en: He encourages them to be faithful in their service, for which they will receive their reward in eternity, when Christ appears, the Chief Shepherd and just Judge, and gives them the crowns of eternal heaven, unlike the glories of earth, which fade away.

5.3.1.en: Take care to serve everyone around you, especially if you have responsibility for others, knowing that your love and labor are very precious to God and He will reward you for them in heaven.

5.4.0.en: He advises the young with a group of commandments, which are:

5.4.1.en: 1- Humility and submission: they submit and obey the priests and the elderly, and indeed they also submit to one another with humility, because God gives grace to the humble and, on the contrary, rejects and resists the proud.

5.5.0.en: He encourages the young to be humble, whether toward their elders or toward one another, for this is a proof of their humility before God, and a great reward awaits them, which is that God supports them in afflictions and comforts their hearts so that they rise above the affliction while they are in it, and then lifts them up on the last day to the heavenly glories and compensates them for all their endurance during their humility.

5.6.0.en: 2- Relying on God: trust in God's love and power, so we place all our problems and needs before Him, and in His fatherhood He cares for us, supplies all our needs and solves our problems.

5.7.0.en: 3- Spiritual vigilance: he calls them to constant spiritual attention and watchfulness, because the devil, our enemy, tries to seize any opportunity to make us fall into sin. He likens him to a lion for his ferocity, but he is unable to harm us; he goes around everywhere and tries to make us fall, but he cannot so long as we are spiritually vigilant and hold fast to God.

5.8.0.en: 4- Spiritual striving: he calls us to resist the devil with all the exercises of spiritual striving, holding fast to our faith however our weakness appears or our sins multiply, especially since the devil fights all people in the world, but believers are distinguished by the grace of God that supports them. If our unbelieving brethren in the world try to reject sins, then all the more we believers, who rely on the power of God, resist him and triumph over him.

5.9.0.en: He encourages them to carry out the preceding commandments, reminding them of the heavenly glories that God has prepared for them because they endured and suffered for His sake in their spiritual striving, and he also promises them that He will:

5.9.1.en: 1- Perfect every lack and weakness in them.

5.9.3.en: 3- Strengthen them against the wars of the devil.

5.9.4.en: 4- Enable them for every good work.

5.9.5.en: And then they glorify God, to whom belong power and dominion over all creatures forever.

5.9.6.en: Be confident that your love and labor for the sake of God have a great reward, and He also supports you in carrying out His commandments. So take courage, however great your weakness and however much the devil's wars increase, because God loves you and perfects you by His grace until you obtain His heavenly glories.

5.10.0.en: Silvanus: known by the name Silas (Acts 15:22), who accompanied Paul on his second missionary journey (Acts 15:40) and wrote the First and Second Epistles to the Thessalonians (1 Thess 1:1, 2 Thess 1:1) and served with Timothy in Corinth (2 Cor 1:19). He was with Mark the Apostle in Egypt and wrote this epistle for the Apostle Peter because of his mastery of Greek, and Peter describes him as faithful because of his commitment and his bearing the responsibilities of the ministry.

5.10.1.en: As I suppose: this does not mean doubt, and in the Greek language it means certainty.

5.10.2.en: The Apostle Peter declares that he dictated his epistle to Silvanus because he is skilled in Greek, and he also sent it with his own hand, so that it includes these sermons and counsels that establish believers in the grace of God. The Apostle Peter condensed these sermons into these words, but he has much more that he wants to say.

5.11.0.en: Babylon: Babylon of the Stairs (Babylon el-Darag) in ancient Egypt, in Egypt.

5.11.1.en: The elect: the Church in Egypt, which St. Mark founded.

5.11.2.en: Peter wrote his epistle in Babylon in ancient Egypt, so he sends the greetings of the Church of Egypt to the churches of the world, and this Church is chosen by God together with the rest of the churches. He also sends the greetings of the founder of this Church, who is Mark the Apostle, and he describes him as his son because he is younger than he, and also his relative, since he is the husband of the daughter of the paternal uncle of the father of Mark the Apostle.

5.12.0.en: In conclusion he asks all believers to deal with one another in peace, and he also sends them his personal peace, filled with love and fatherhood.

5.12.1.en: Offer words of love and peace to everyone you meet, so that you absorb the agitation and tension in him, win him, and show Christ to him.
